summary: A modal window for a short, focused task that must be finished or cancelled before the user goes back to the page: rename a token, invite a reviewer, review a release.
whenToUse: A task of one to three fields that belongs to the current page and needs the user's full attention.
Reviewing something before committing it, like release notes before Publish.
Size sm for one field, md (default) for short forms, lg for reading or comparing content.
whenNotToUse: Confirming a destructive action: use AlertDialog, which cannot be dismissed by clicking outside.
Details the user wants to read next to the page, like a token's history: use Drawer.
A hint or a small menu anchored to a control: use Popover or Menu.
Long multi-step flows: give them a page. Stacked dialogs lose people.

dos.title: Title says the task, the primary button repeats the verb
dos.text: "Rename token" opens a dialog titled "Rename token" whose primary action is "Rename token". Users always know where they are.

dos.title: Keep the footer for actions only
dos.text: Alternatives first, primary last, aligned to the end. Explanations go in the description or the body.

donts.title: A dialog for information the page could show inline
donts.text: Interrupting to say "Saved" costs a click. Use a Toast or an inline Alert.

donts.title: Vague footer labels
donts.text: "OK" and "Yes" make users reread the title to know what they agree to.

accessibility: Base UI Dialog: role dialog, aria-modal, named by the title and described by the description.
Focus moves into the dialog when it opens (the first focusable element, or initialFocus) and is trapped there.
Escape, the close button and a click on the scrim close it; focus returns to the trigger.
The page behind is inert and scroll is locked while the dialog is open.
The body scrolls on its own when content is long, so the title and the actions stay visible.
Motion is a 200ms fade and a slight rise; with reduced motion it appears instantly.
contentGuidelines: Title: the task as a verb phrase in sentence case, no period: "Invite reviewer".
Description: one or two sentences on what happens next. Skip it if the title says enough.
Primary button repeats the title's verb. Secondary is "Cancel".
The close button label says what it closes: "Close dialog".
